scorecards.inningsCommentary: Australia commenced their first innings at Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 111 from Steve Smith, complemented by a commanding 134-run stand between Steve Smith and David Warner that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.39 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Kuldeep Yadav (4/68), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 300/10 (88.3 ov), Australia posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

Reaching 332/10 (118.1 ov), India's innings completed the first-innings exchange (32 Runs (India)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: India embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 106 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. KL Rahul anchored the innings with a resolute 51, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. Pat Cummins (2/42) maintained tight lines for Australia, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Reaching 106/2 (23.5 ov), India successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

summaryTab.matchStory: Australia built a commanding first-innings platform of 300, spearheaded by Steve Smith's brilliant 111. Nathan Lyon's 5-wicket haul dismantled India for 332, handing the advantage to Australia. Australia posted 137 in their second innings, shifting match momentum decisively through crucial partnerships. India held their nerve in the fourth-innings chase, reaching the target to seal a famous victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 300/10 (88.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 332/10 (118.1 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 127 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Ravindra Jadeja delivered a masterclass for India (63 Runs & 4 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 52%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Australia faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by R Ashwin (30 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 8 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Australia produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
